---
title: "07_analysis_3"
format: html
---

Goal - examine combinations of several characteristics within the same patients
and see if particular combinations have impact on deaths

Library
```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(ggplot2)
library(patchwork)
library(broom)
```

Load clean data
```{r}
clean_data <- read_tsv(file = "data/03_dat_aug.tsv", show_col_types = FALSE)
```

Convert binary values into categorical
```{r}
categorical_data <- clean_data |>
  mutate(
    diabetes = factor(
      diabetes,
      levels = c(0, 1),
      labels = c("no", "yes")
    ),
    chf = factor(
      chf,
      levels = c(0, 1),
      labels = c("no", "yes")
    )
  )
```

Identify categorical variables
```{r}
categorical_cols <- categorical_data |>
  select(where(is.character) | where(is.factor)) |>
  names()
```

Calculating mortality percentage

```{r}
mortality_summary <- categorical_data |>
  select(death, sex, race, smoker, chf, diabetes) |>
  mutate(across(-death, as.character)) |>
  pivot_longer(
    cols = -death, names_to = "variable", values_to = "category"
  ) |>
  drop_na(category, death) |>
  group_by(variable, category) |>
  summarise(
    n = n(),
    n_deaths = sum(death == 1),
    percent_death = 100 * mean(death == 1),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

mortality_summary
```

Selecting top five characteristics
```{r}
top5 <- mortality_summary |>
  filter(n >= 15) |>
  arrange(desc(percent_death)) |>
  slice_head(n = 5)

top5
```

Visualizing
```{r}
top5_plot <- top5 |>
  mutate(
    characteristic = paste(variable, category, sep = ": ")
  ) |>
  ggplot(aes(
    x = reorder(characteristic, percent_death),
    y = percent_death
  )) +
  geom_col(fill = "steelblue", width = 0.6) +
  geom_text(
    aes(label = paste0(
      round(percent_death, 1), "%"
    )),
    hjust = -0.2,
    size = 4
  ) +
  coord_flip() +
  scale_y_continuous(
    expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.2))
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Top 5 characteristics by mortality",
    x = NULL,
    y = "Mortality (%)"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

top5_plot
```

As we see that smoking alone is not statistically significant cause of death
but patients who smoke still experience high death rates. Maybe people who die
from chf or diabetes also smoke and it works in combination?

Preparing data
```{r}
profile_data <- clean_data |>
  mutate(
    smoking_group = if_else(
      packyrs > 0,
      "Smoking exposure",
      "No smoking exposure"
    ),
    chf_group = if_else(
      chf == 1,
      "CHF",
      "No CHF"
    ),
    diabetes_group = if_else(
      diabetes == 1,
      "Diabetes",
      "No diabetes"
    )
  )
```


Combining smoking and CHF

```{r}
chf_summary <- profile_data |>
  drop_na(smoking_group, chf_group, death) |>
  group_by(smoking_group, chf_group) |>
  summarise(
    n = n(),
    n_deaths = sum(death == 1),
    percent_death = 100 * mean(death == 1),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  arrange(desc(percent_death))

chf_summary
```


Visualizing
```{r}
chf_plot <- chf_summary |>
  ggplot(aes(
    x = chf_group,
    y = percent_death,
    fill = smoking_group
  )) +
  geom_col(position = "dodge", width = 0.7) +
  geom_text(
    aes(label = paste0(round(percent_death, 1), "%")),
    position = position_dodge(width = 0.7),
    vjust = -0.4,
    size = 4
  ) +
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = c(
      "No smoking exposure" = "steelblue",
      "Smoking exposure" = "tomato"
    )
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.15))
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Mortality by smoking exposure and CHF",
    x = "CHF status",
    y = "Mortality (%)",
    fill = "Smoking status"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

chf_plot

ggsave(
  "results/07_analysis_3/smoking_chf.png",
  chf_plot,
  width = 8,
  height = 6,
  dpi = 300
)
```
We see that people who smoke and have CHF experience most of the deaths


Diabetes and smoking combination:
```{r}
diabetes_summary <- profile_data |>
  drop_na(smoking_group, diabetes_group, death) |>
  group_by(smoking_group, diabetes_group) |>
  summarise(
    n = n(),
    n_deaths = sum(death == 1),
    percent_death = 100 * mean(death == 1),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  arrange(desc(percent_death))

diabetes_summary
```


Vizualizing:
```{r}
diabetes_plot <- diabetes_summary |>
  ggplot(aes(
    x = diabetes_group,
    y = percent_death,
    fill = smoking_group
  )) +
  geom_col(position = "dodge", width = 0.7) +
  geom_text(
    aes(label = paste0(round(percent_death, 1), "%")),
    position = position_dodge(width = 0.7),
    vjust = -0.4,
    size = 4
  ) +
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = c(
      "No smoking exposure" = "steelblue",
      "Smoking exposure" = "tomato"
    )
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.15))
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Mortality by smoking exposure and diabetes",
    x = "Diabetes status",
    y = "Mortality (%)",
    fill = "Smoking status"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

diabetes_plot

ggsave(
  "results/07_analysis_3/smoking_diabetes.png",
  diabetes_plot,
  width = 8,
  height = 6,
  dpi = 300
)
```


Combining graphs:
```{r}

combined_mortality_plot <- wrap_plots(
  chf_plot,
  diabetes_plot,
  ncol = 2
) +
  plot_annotation(
    title = "Smoking exposure and clinical conditions"
  )

combined_mortality_plot

ggsave(
  "results/07_analysis_3/combined_mortality_plot.png",
  combined_mortality_plot,
  width = 14,
  height = 6,
  dpi = 300
)
```
